title: The lead agent builds when told to: an order, a bare yes and 'you decide' are read as a person says them (the owner's second Telco session)
request: The owner kept going in the same draft after the act-first fixes and asked for a model: five messages and three questions to start one build, 'Can you reply build the model so I can start it?', then the build asked for the outcome column again, and 'you decide' drew another report. 'Now go on to make fixes.' Budget: the $2 the owner gave.
spec: An order to build a model, a bare yes to the agent's own question and 'you decide' are the person's decisions; the build starts in the same turn with the outcome column the person already named or confirmed; no report is drawn in a turn about a model; a chart says what a count counts.
plan: read the saved case events and case file of the owner's draft
fix the build request: a whole short message is a valid quote, an order to build is a yes, delegation is a go-ahead
carry the confirmed outcome column into the build
refuse report cards while the work is a model
name the condition in a conditional count's title and header
scripted replay tests, one live replay of the whole session

decisions.decision: An explicit order to build a model skips the readiness interview; a plain yes still needs a ready case
decisions.why: the live replay showed the agent refusing to request the build until the decision and the user were said, after the person had ordered it twice; the build's own questions (outcome, prediction moment said back) remain the guard

decisions.decision: The outcome column is taken only from the person's words or an assumption they confirmed
decisions.why: the api rule says DCLab does not pick the outcome for the person; a column they named is theirs

decisions.decision: Decision questions are refused by code after an order or a delegation
decisions.why: asking what they will do with a model they ordered twice was the stall the owner objected to

change: dclab_rnd/agents/case_agent.py (_request_build, ORDER_MODEL, DELEGATE, orders_model, _model_work, _ask), dclab_core/case.py (whole_short_message, grounded_columns), dclab_rnd/draft/case_home.py (_build, _outcome_candidates, _build_answer), dclab_rnd/home_query.py and home_chart.py (conditional count text), dclab_rnd/agents/case_session.py (budget text), dclab_rnd/prompts/case_agent.md, scripts/live_home_telco_replay.py, tests.

findings.defect: A bare yes could never start a build
findings.scenario: the agent asked 'Shall I build it now?', the person said yes, the agent answered 'Can you reply build the model so I can start it?'
findings.cause: quote_ok needs two words and the case file applied the same rule to the build's quote
findings.fix: the quote may be the whole of a short message (core whole_short_message), in the agent's check and in the case file's

findings.defect: 'build the model' and 'make prediction models' were not a yes or a go-ahead
findings.scenario: the person ordered a model twice and was asked 'Shall I build it now?' each time
findings.cause: BUILD_YES and GO_AHEAD named only 'build it' and 'go ahead'
findings.fix: orders_model and DELEGATE; a question about building stays no yes

findings.defect: The outcome the person had confirmed was asked again with an example from another table
findings.scenario: 'Which column is the outcome ... for example the outcome is is_fraud' after 'Churn means the customer left' was confirmed
findings.cause: nothing carried a confirmed column into understanding.target; the example text is fixed
findings.fix: request_build takes an outcome that code grounds in the person's words; CaseHome writes it before the build; the question names the table's own candidates; 'you decide' uses the one grounded column

findings.defect: A report was drawn again in a turn about a model, and 'you decide' drew one
findings.scenario: 'now build model' answered with a report and a dashboard; 'you decide' answered 'I've decided to give you the report you asked for first'
findings.cause: nothing refused a card while the work was a model
findings.fix: _model_work refuses answer and dashboard cards unless the message asks for figures

findings.defect: A chart of customers lost was titled 'Number of rows by Contract'
findings.scenario: a count with a condition drawn with the title and header of an unconditional count
findings.cause: describe and spec ignored the count's where
findings.fix: the title and header carry the condition; the model's own text names only the column

findings.defect: The live replay still stalled on the build: the agent refused to request it until the decision and the user were said
findings.scenario: 'now build model' answered 'DCLab won't build it yet because it needs to know what you'll do with the scores'; 'make prediction models' and 'yes' got the same question
findings.cause: _request_build required a ready case for every yes
findings.fix: an order to build skips the interview; a decision question is refused after an order

findings.defect: The case budget message said 'budget of EUR 0' for a cap under one euro
A negated, delayed or reported 'build a model' was read as an order and started a build
findings.scenario: 'I won't build a model until you show me churn by contract' passed the yes check and skipped the readiness gate
findings.cause: orders_model rejected only a question mark, a leading question word and a few delay words
findings.fix: an order must open with the verb, be short and hold no negation or delay; refusals and delays veto a go-ahead; 'no model please, whatever you think' is no delegation

findings.defect: A column only mentioned could become the outcome, and a bare yes to another question could request a build
findings.scenario: 'Is it different by gender?' made gender the target when it was the only two-valued column named; a yes to 'Want me to also show churn by contract?' could request the build
findings.cause: grounding was a whole-word match anywhere in the history, including the agent's paraphrases; a one-word quote checked nothing about the question asked
findings.fix: a column is grounded only in a sentence of the person's own words (or a confirmed assumption) that also holds outcome language; a bare yes needs the agent's last message to have asked about building

findings.defect: The report block was too wide: a mention of risk, or a yes to an offered chart, drew nothing
findings.scenario: 'Which contract has the highest churn risk? chart it' got the model-work refusal
findings.cause: _model_work counted any model word and any yes
findings.fix: only an order to build, a delegation, or a build route with no figures request blocks a card

measurements.name: owner's whole session replayed live (run2: report half and build half)
measurements.gate: practice scorecard of 2026-11-02 (acts when asked, no stalling)
measurements.result: the report half: figures at the second message, dashboards drawn, no stalling phrase; the build half did not start the build (fixed afterwards)
limits: the soft cap of the run was reached on the last message
the fix for the readiness gate has scripted tests only, no live run

outcome: The report half of the owner's session works live. The build half was fixed in two rounds: the first (a bare yes, orders, the confirmed outcome, no redrawn report) is covered by scripted tests; the live replay then showed one more gate (readiness before the build request), fixed after it and again covered by scripted tests only. The test budget is spent: a live replay of the build half is still owed. A second independent review found five safety and behaviour defects in the first version of this package; all five are fixed and covered by tests.
lessons: a person's one-word yes must be quotable: a rule written for facts (two words of evidence) must not gate a decision
an order is an order: asking whether to build after the person ordered it twice reads as stalling however polite
when a live run shows another gate, the scripted test must follow the live message, not the author's guess of it
risks: the build half is not proven live
treating 'build model' as a yes removes a confirmation; the build's outcome and prediction-moment questions remain the guard
